newsitem.title: USA: US mayors take up brownfield, clean water policies.
newsitem.headline: US mayors take up brownfield, clean water policies.

text.p: U.S. mayors meeting here on Tuesday are expected to urge the U.S. Congress to reauthorize landmark water cleanup legislation, to fund water infrastructure programs, and set up a broad "brownfields" strategy.

The resolutions are among dozens approved on Saturday by committees of the U.S. Conference of Mayors which is holding its 65th annual conference here this week. Mayors are expected to adopt the proposals at an open meeting tomorrow.
Brownfields are pieces of lightly contaminated land in urban centers that do not qualify for Superfund toxic waste cleanup funding.
A mayors' committee voted on Saturday to urge Congress to adopt broad legislation giving cities tools they need to clean up and redevelop blighted sites.
Legislation should include tax incentives to stimulate private investment in cleanup efforts, including expanded use of tax-exempt bond financing, the mayors' panel said.

A mayors' panel this weekend also called for continued funding of the Clean Water and Drinking Water State Revolving Funds at least at levels proposed by the Clinton Administration for the next five years.
